name: toolrow-intentless-hit-area
description: An intent-less expandable ToolRow keeps its visible summary line and its inline controls as SIBLINGS of the disclosure button, and the button still owns the whole row: toolcallitem.module.css's .row:not([data-intent="true"]) .trigger overlay (position: absolute; inset: 0) covers the summary line, the summary line itself ignores pointer input, and real links and buttons inside it opt back in. So a click on plain summary text reaches the disclosure trigger, a click on the summary's link reaches the link, and a click on an inline Open control reaches that control. Two shapes, both ToolRow's current render copied from its jsdom output: web_fetch's linked summary ('Fetched url') and a write row with a trailing OpenButton. These hit-area checks lived inside the deleted rdry-toolrow-contrast case; no other case covers intent-less rows.

mutation.declaration: toolcallitem.module.css: .row:not([data-intent="true"]) .trigger { position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; justify-content: flex-end } (rule deleted)
mutation.note: Three rules mutated one at a time, each restored before the next. Deleting the .trigger overlay fails both fixtures: the trigger no longer covers the row or the summary, and plain summary text lands on div.row. Dropping the summary line's pointer-events: none fails both with plain text landing on the summary span instead of the trigger. Dropping the a/button pointer-events: auto rule fails both with the link and the Open control swallowed by the trigger (button#trigger-web, svg inside button#trigger-write). The deleted rdry-toolrow-contrast harness failed the first mutation too (triggerContainsSummary and summaryHitTrigger false), and no other case failed it.
